content.text:
I cleaned up `0.html` without changing how it looks: it's still a black circle centered on the page. I haven't opened it in a browser.

- **No stray scrollbars:** `width: 100vw` can make the page scroll sideways when a vertical scrollbar is showing, so I removed it. The body now uses `min-height` instead of a fixed `height`.
- **Mobile height:** I added `100dvh`, which keeps the circle centered correctly on mobile browsers where the address bar shrinks the visible area. Older browsers fall back to `100vh`.
- **Fits small screens:** the SVG is now `min(400px, 100vmin)`, so it shrinks on screens smaller than 400px instead of getting cut off. On larger screens it stays 400px.
- **Simpler centering:** I swapped the three flexbox rules for two grid rules (`display: grid; place-items: center`). I also added `display: block` to the SVG to remove the small gap browsers leave under inline elements.
- **Screen readers:** the SVG now has `role="img"` and a `<title>`, so screen readers can announce it. Right now they skip it.
- **Box sizing:** I added `box-sizing: border-box` to the reset, which makes sizes easier to predict if you add more content later.

I kept the `id` and page title as they are, since they look like generated identifiers. If you meant a different kind of improvement, such as visual changes, animation or dark mode, tell me which.
